indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B5.4.2.1 Describe the likelihood of a single outcome occurring using words such as impossible, possible, and certain
indicator.objective: Classify the likelihood of a single outcome occurring in a probability experiment as impossible, possible, or certain

skills.description: Classify outcomes as impossible, possible (likely/unlikely), or certain.
Give examples of impossible, possible, and certain events.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Not recognising that an event can be possible but unlikely.

questions.stem: A bag contains only red balls. If you pick one ball without looking, what is the likelihood of picking a red ball?
hints: Every ball in the bag is red.
questions.explanation: It is certain because all the balls are red.
questions.misconception: Saying possible because you cannot see the ball.

questions.stem: A bag contains only red balls. What is the likelihood of picking a blue ball?
hints: There are no blue balls in the bag.
questions.explanation: It is impossible because there are no blue balls.
questions.misconception: Saying possible because blue is a colour.

options: You will see a lion in Accra
You will roll a 7 on a normal die
hints: Certain means it will definitely happen.
questions.explanation: The sun rising tomorrow is certain.
questions.misconception: Choosing rain because it often rains.

options: Rolling a 6 on a normal die
Rolling a 7 on a normal die
Picking a red ball from a bag of red balls
Tossing a coin and getting heads
hints: A normal die has numbers 1 to 6.
questions.explanation: Rolling a 7 on a normal die is impossible.
questions.misconception: Choosing rolling a 6 because it is hard.

questions.stem: A bag has 10 red balls and 1 green ball. Picking a red ball is:
hints: There are red balls and green balls.
questions.explanation: Picking a red ball is possible, and it is likely.
questions.misconception: Saying certain because there are many red balls.

questions.stem: A spinner has 4 equal sectors: red, blue, green, yellow. Landing on red is:
hints: Red is one of the sectors.
questions.misconception: Saying impossible because there are other colours.

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 green balls and 5 yellow balls. Picking a green ball is:
hints: There are green balls in the bag.
questions.explanation: It is possible to pick a green ball.
questions.misconception: Saying certain because half are green.

questions.stem: Give one example of an impossible event in Ghana.
answer: seeing a lion in the classroom
hints: Think of something that cannot happen.
questions.explanation: For example, snow falling in Accra is impossible.
questions.misconception: Giving an unlikely but possible event.

questions.stem: Give one example of a certain event in your school day.
answer: the teacher will come to class
the sun will shine during the day
hints: Certain means it will definitely happen.
questions.explanation: For example, the school bell ringing is certain.
questions.misconception: Giving an event that only sometimes happens.

questions.stem: A bag has 3 red balls, 3 blue balls, and 3 green balls. Picking a yellow ball is:
questions.explanation: Picking a yellow ball is impossible.
questions.misconception: Saying possible because yellow is a colour.

questions.stem: A coin is tossed. Landing on heads is:
hints: A coin has heads and tails.
questions.misconception: Saying certain because it is one of the sides.

questions.stem: Explain why picking a black ball from a bag containing only white balls is impossible.
hints: Look at the colours in the bag.
questions.explanation: It is impossible because there are no black balls in the bag.

criteria.description: States there are no black balls.

questions.misconception: Thinking black is possible because it is a colour.

questions.stem: A bag has 20 red balls and 1 blue ball. Picking a blue ball is:
hints: There is only one blue ball.
questions.misconception: Saying impossible because there is only one.

questions.stem: A bag has 20 red balls and 1 blue ball. Picking a red ball is:
questions.explanation: Picking a red ball is likely, but not certain.
questions.misconception: Saying certain because most are red.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between an impossible event and an unlikely event.
hints: Impossible cannot happen; unlikely can happen but rarely.
questions.explanation: An impossible event cannot happen at all. An unlikely event can happen, but it has a very small chance.

questions.stem: A pupil says 'If an event is possible, it must be likely.' Is the pupil correct? Explain with an example.
questions.explanation: No. An event can be possible but unlikely, such as picking the one blue ball from a bag of 20 red balls.

criteria.description: Gives a possible but unlikely example.

questions.stem: Describe an experiment where an outcome is certain.
hints: All possible outcomes must be the same.
questions.explanation: For example, a bag containing only red balls: picking a red ball is certain.

criteria.description: Describes an experiment with only one outcome type.

questions.misconception: Describing an experiment with mixed outcomes.

questions.stem: A bag has 2 red, 2 blue, and 2 green balls. A pupil says picking a red ball is certain because there are red balls. Explain the mistake.
hints: Certain means it must happen every time.
questions.explanation: The pupil is incorrect. Picking a red ball is possible, but not certain, because there are also blue and green balls.

criteria.description: Explains red is possible but not certain.

questions.misconception: Thinking presence of red makes it certain.

questions.stem: Create one impossible event and one certain event related to a football match.
hints: Impossible: score without kicking? Certain: match has a start.
questions.explanation: Impossible: a player scores with no ball. Certain: the match will have a beginning.
